title: Bypassed

brief.story: A customer’s night light is dark, but the resistor is warm. Nothing is burnt, nothing is backwards. Something is letting the current skip the LED.
brief.goal: Find the short and fix it so LED1 carries 15–25 mA.

hints: Measure across LED1: a lit LED has about 2 V across it. 0 V means both its legs are at the same voltage, joined by something else.
Follow the wires: W2 should take LED1’s short leg (column 13) to ground. Where does it actually start?
W2 starts in column 10, LED1’s long leg, so it shorts the LED out. Move it to column 13.

spec.explain: A wire across a part is a short: the current takes the wire, and the part gets nothing.

debrief: A short is a path with (almost) no resistance around a part. The current takes it, the part gets 0 V and does nothing, and everything before it runs hotter. 0 V across a part that should be working is the meter’s way of saying “short”. It’s the commonest fault on a hand-built board: one wire in the wrong column.
